atomic_proposition: Home insurance may not cover business stock kept at home.
source_name: GOV.UK — Running a business from home
verbatim_supporting_passage: Home insurance may not cover your business (such as stock, computers, customers visiting your premises).
passage_location: Insurance section, first paragraph, second sentence. Browser text line 65 on retrieval.
scope: UK home-based businesses; possibility of a gap in household cover, not a finding about any policy.
limitations: The word may is essential. This does not say every home policy excludes stock, or that this consumer is uninsured. Obtain applicable wording, schedule and endorsements or insurer confirmation.
retrieval_tags: home business, business stock, garage, automatic cover

atomic_proposition: Some home insurance policies cover business equipment at home and others do not.
source_name: MoneyHelper — Business insurance when you’re self employed
verbatim_supporting_passage: Even though some home insurance policies will cover business equipment in your home, not all do
passage_location: Running a business from home, second bullet, excerpt from second sentence. Browser text line 33.
scope: UK household business-equipment guidance; equipment only.
limitations: Equipment is not a synonym for merchandise or stock. The surrounding page discusses clerical use; do not export its categorical visitor wording as a universal policy rule. This record neither proves stock cover nor establishes a legal duty to volunteer every fact.
retrieval_tags: home office, equipment, clerical, policy variation

atomic_proposition: Aviva’s July 2026 home insurance IPID states that business or professional property is not covered, except home office equipment or where Aviva has specifically agreed otherwise.
source_name: Aviva Insurance Limited — Home Insurance IPID
verbatim_supporting_passage: We don’t cover property which is used for a business or profession (except home office equipment) unless we have specifically agreed to do so.
passage_location: PDF page 2 of 2, Are there any restrictions on cover?, second ! bullet. Footer NHDHG15501 07.2026. Browser text lines 130–132.
scope: Only the Aviva home insurance product summary actually retrieved, with Aviva, Aviva Gold and Aviva Platinum tiers; illustrative restriction, not all Aviva products.
limitations: An IPID is a summary, not the complete contract. Preserve both the home-office-equipment exception and specific-agreement exception. No consumer schedule, endorsements, equipment definition or agreement was examined. The URL is dynamic: search metadata mentioned older Online/Premium branding, whereas the opened document identifies the July 2026 product.
retrieval_tags: business property, stock exclusion, home office equipment, specific agreement, Aviva

atomic_proposition: An item that can reasonably be removed and taken to another home is usually contents and generally not covered by a buildings policy.
source_name: Financial Ombudsman Service — Home and buildings insurance
verbatim_supporting_passage: then it’s usually part of the contents and won’t generally be covered by a buildings policy.
passage_location: What is home and buildings insurance? > What buildings insurance covers, second paragraph; quoted clause follows the condition about reasonably removing the item to another home. Browser text line 70.
scope: UK home-insurance buildings/contents distinction; removable items generally.
limitations: Usually and generally are essential qualifications. Application to movable garage stock is an inference, not a policy decision. A garage structure being insured does not establish that its stored goods are insured. No contents policy is thereby shown to cover business stock.

atomic_proposition: ABI guidance says to insure stock at its cost price rather than its sale price when taking out commercial contents insurance.
source_name: Association of British Insurers — Commercial property insurance
verbatim_supporting_passage: If you are taking out contents insurance you should insure stock against its cost price, not its sale price.
passage_location: Contents insurance section, second paragraph, first sentence. Browser text line 31. Earlier products-and-issues URL redirects to this canonical URL.
scope: UK commercial contents stock valuation guidance; stock rather than premises rebuild or business equipment.
limitations: General valuation guidance, not a binding settlement formula for every contract. Confirm the stock definition, valuation basis, sum insured and applicable terms. Do not treat lost retail margin as insured stock value.
retrieval_tags: stock value, cost price, retail price, sum insured

atomic_proposition: Hiscox describes its business contents insurance as potentially helping with the cost of repairing or replacing equipment and stock.
verbatim_supporting_passage: Hiscox business contents insurance can help with the cost of repairing or replacing equipment and stock.
passage_location: Opening section under Business contents insurance, third paragraph before the quote link. Browser text line 17.
scope: Hiscox UK commercial contents product description; potential cover only.
limitations: Marketing description, not full wording or confirmation that a home garage, occupation, stock type or consumer is accepted. This establishes a potential commercial-cover route, not a product recommendation or evidence that an ordinary household policy covers stock.
retrieval_tags: business contents, stock cover, equipment, Hiscox

atomic_proposition: AXA’s UK stock-insurance page advertises a 30% seasonal cover increase during November and December.
source_name: AXA UK — Business Stock & Contents Insurance
verbatim_supporting_passage: 30% during the months of November and December
passage_location: What is a seasonal cover increase?, numbered item 1. Browser text line 753.
scope: Only the AXA UK business stock offering described on this page; a product-specific seasonal increase.
limitations: Not a UK-wide 30% rule and not an increase in ordinary home insurance. The page also describes another bank-holiday period and an option to amend dates. This excerpt alone does not establish contractual eligibility, adequacy at peak stock value, or any consumer’s dates or limit.
retrieval_tags: seasonal stock, peak value, November, December, AXA

atomic_proposition: ABI lists running a business from home with professional visitors as a situation in which to consider public liability insurance.
source_name: Association of British Insurers — Public liability insurance
verbatim_supporting_passage: You run a business from your home and people visit your home for professional purposes
passage_location: Buying public liability insurance, third bullet following You should consider public liability insurance if:. Browser text lines 39–45; quoted text at line 45.
scope: UK home business with professional visitors; public liability consideration, separate from stock property cover.
limitations: Consider does not mean universally compulsory. A visitor fact is a context question, not evidence of liability, lack of cover, or a recommendation of a particular contract. Do not infer that public liability replaces stock insurance.
retrieval_tags: customer visits, client visits, public liability, home business

atomic_proposition: Flood Re’s eligibility criteria include the property having been built before 1 January 2009.
source_name: Flood Re — Qualifying policies which may be ceded to Flood Re
passage_location: Qualifying policies which may be ceded to Flood Re, criterion 7; excerpt before the parenthesis. Browser text line 9.
scope: UK Flood Re scheme eligibility, secondary tests only; one criterion of eight.
limitations: A necessary criterion is not sufficient eligibility. Criterion 7 retains eligibility for a home built before the cutoff then demolished and rebuilt. Other criteria and the distinction between contents and buildings must be checked. A new post-2008 home and a rebuilt qualifying home are not equivalent. No business-stock coverage follows.
retrieval_tags: Flood Re, 2009, eligibility, new build, rebuild

atomic_proposition: Insurers choose whether to reinsure an eligible property through Flood Re.
verbatim_supporting_passage: However, it’s the insurers that choose whether or not to reinsure that property through us.
passage_location: Could my property qualify for Flood Re?, paragraph immediately after the general-guide explanation. Browser text line 9.
scope: UK Flood Re reinsurance discretion; secondary tests only.
limitations: Eligibility does not guarantee an insurance offer or use of Flood Re. This is not a full eligibility assessment or evidence of business-stock cover. Do not infer that working from home alone either qualifies or disqualifies a property.
retrieval_tags: Flood Re, guarantee, insurer choice, reinsurance
